newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: POSCO begins JV construction in Brazil.
newsitem.headline: POSCO begins JV construction in Brazil.

text.p: South Korea's Pohang Iron and Steel Co (POSCO), the world's second largest steelmaker, said on Wednesday it had started construction of its joint venture iron pellet plant in Brazil.

The company spokesaman said POSCO and Companhia Valedo Rio Doce, a Brazilian iron ore exporter, had signed the 50-50 joint venture deal in September 1995. The venture, named Kobrasco, was capitalised at $77 million.
He said the venture would invest $220 million by 1998 to complete the plant near Rio De Janeiro. It will have an annual production capacity of four million tonnes of pellets.
Of the total, 2.3 million tonnes would be imported to South Korea and the remaining 1.7 million would be used by the Brazilian company.
The pellets, made of iron ore powder, limestone and other ingredients, are used as a substitute for iron ore to produce crude steel.
